working_title: Ep 48: The No-Show Fix With Jordan Lee

facts.fact: Wrote that missed bookings fell from 14% to 4% after deposits and new reminders (post dated 2025-10-08)
Takes a deposit only on long appointments and first visits

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Welcome to The Slotkeeper Podcast, the show for people who run salons, clinics and studios. I'm Casey Reed.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Today's guest runs Northside Hair Studio, and her no-show numbers are the best I've seen from a small salon.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Jordan, welcome. How did no-shows become your thing?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: By accident, really. I shared our numbers in a group for salon owners and people kept asking how.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Before you changed anything, what were no-shows costing you?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: We were losing about 14% of booked appointments, and on a color booking that is a three hour hole in the day.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: When I added it up it was um close to one stylist's wages every single month.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: You talked about deposits on Shearline Talk last year, when you'd just started. What has changed since then?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: The biggest change is that we stopped taking a deposit on every booking. Now it's only appointments over 90 minutes and first visits.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: A deposit on a 20 minute fringe trim just annoys people, and those clients were showing up anyway.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: How big is the deposit now?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: It's 25% of the service price, and it comes off the bill, so it never feels like a fee.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Did you lose clients when the deposits started?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: We lost a handful in the first month. Most of them came back within the year.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: I wrote the whole thing up in the deposit post on our blog, with the exact wording we use at booking.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Let's talk reminders. When do your reminder texts go out?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: Two of them. One 48 hours before, so there's still time to fill the slot, and one on the morning of the appointment.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: The 48 hour one is the one that matters. A cancellation two days out is a slot we can sell again.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: What does the text actually say?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: It says the time, the stylist, and one line: reply C to cancel, no call needed. Making it easy to cancel is what fills the book.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: Clients who can cancel in two seconds tell you. Clients who have to phone just don't come.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: With the deposits and the new reminders together, we're um down to 4% from 14%.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: What about clients who turn up late?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: We give 15 minutes. After that we offer to shorten the service or move it, and the client chooses.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: Never make a late client feel like a problem in front of the whole salon. Have that talk at the desk, quietly.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Do you charge for lateness?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: No. We copied the cancellation policy template from Example Booking Software and took the late fee out.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: If a listener could change one thing this week, what should it be?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: Send the reminder 48 hours out instead of 24, and let people cancel by text. That alone moved us from 14% to 9%.

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: Then read The Gapwell Ledger. It changed how I think about every gap in the book.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: Where can people find you and the studio?

lines.speaker: Jordan
lines.text: Northside Hair Studio is on Instagram and our website, and the deposit post is still the most read page we have.

lines.speaker: Casey
lines.text: That's the episode. Next week we're on front desk hiring. Thanks for listening to The Slotkeeper Podcast.
